title: Horizon boundary mechanics: from one potential to horizon work

source.title: Horizon boundary mechanics — Area, acceleration length, and horizon work (one-page summary)

selectedInputs.title: Selected Einstein boundary potential
selectedInputs.statement: For a prescribed clock and the stated Einstein boundary prescription, U(A,L) = c^4 A / (8 pi G L). Treat this physical starting potential as a cited input; the symbolic checker tests its consequences, not its derivation from the full action.

selectedInputs.title: Positive acceleration-length convention
selectedInputs.statement: The one-page summary specifies positive surface gravity: L = c^2 / kappa, with c and G fixed. Use A > 0 and L > 0. Area and length are independent while taking the common partial derivatives.

selectedInputs.title: Schwarzschild horizon family
selectedInputs.statement: With Killing time normalized at infinity, the one-page summary sets A = 4 pi R^2 and L = 2 R, with R > 0 and areal volume V = 4 pi R^3 / 3. Apply these substitutions after taking the common partial derivatives; distinguish P_R from P_L.

mainClaim: Starting from the selected Einstein boundary potential, one complete differential identifies surface stress and length-conjugate force; force per area gives normal-scale pressure. For the Schwarzschild family, the same work becomes work through the horizon’s own areal radius, with P_R = 2 P_L. These are conditional mathematical consequences of the listed inputs.
assumptions: Use only the author’s one-page summary dated 12 October 2026 as the source of the claims below. This prepared example still requires the author to inspect and approve its formal translation.
c, G, and pi are positive constants. pi denotes the usual mathematical constant. A and L are positive independent variables before specialization; R is a positive areal radius.
Keep the physical clock normalization, orientation, and stated boundary prescription fixed when interpreting the mechanical responses.
Use the definitions Pi = c^4/(8 pi G L), F_L = A c^4/(8 pi G L^2), and P_L = c^4/(8 pi G L^2) as the proposed response formulas to test against derivatives of U.
For the Schwarzschild realization substitute A = 4 pi R^2 and L = 2 R only after computing the independent-variable responses; area and volume then co-vary.

For the final coordinate-change check, take the one-page summary’s selected scalar response (A c^2/(8 pi G)) delta kappa as a cited input, with theta = delta theta = 0, fixed clock and cuts, and the stated mixed boundary prescription.

definitions.description: Positive surface gravity written in acceleration-length coordinates; Eq. (1).
The selected boundary potential supplied as a physical input; Eq. (1).
Proposed area response; checked against the partial derivative of U; Eqs. (2)–(3).
Proposed force response; checked against minus the partial derivative of U; Eqs. (2)–(3).
Proposed force density and stress slope; Eq. (4).
Restrict the potential to the Schwarzschild family A = 4 pi R^2, L = 2 R.
Areal volume; this definition is local to the Schwarzschild family.
Transform the existing length-work coefficient to the actual areal-radius coordinate; Eq. (6).
Radial force divided by the same horizon sphere’s area; Eq. (6).

claims.title: Area response is surface stress
claims.explanation: At fixed L, c, and G, differentiating the input potential with respect to A gives Pi. This checks the dA coefficient of Eq. (2).

claims.title: Length response is minus the force
claims.explanation: At fixed A, c, and G, minus the length derivative gives F_L. Together with the area response this checks the complete differential in Eq. (2).

claims.title: Force density is the squared-acceleration pressure
claims.explanation: The force per area equals kappa squared divided by 8 pi G, as in Eq. (4).

claims.title: Pressure is the negative surface-stress slope
claims.explanation: With the listed constants fixed, dPi = -P_L dL. This is a comparison of boundary configurations, not a new material pressure gradient.

claims.title: Pressure, area, and length recover the same potential
claims.explanation: Eq. (4) identifies U = P_L A L. This product identity does not make A L a geometric volume.

claims.title: Schwarzschild radial pressure is twice the length pressure
claims.explanation: After A = 4 pi R^2 and L = 2 R, changing the work coordinate gives P_R = 2 P_L; Eq. (6).

claims.title: Length work and radial volume work agree
claims.explanation: Equality of the coefficients of dR checks F_L dL = P_R dV on the same Schwarzschild horizon, using its own areal volume.

claims.title: The complete potential law survives the family constraint
claims.explanation: Check dU = Pi dA - P_R dV along the family. Both area and volume change; the work term must not be appended as an independent correction to the usual mass first law.

claims.title: The Schwarzschild potential equals three radial pressure–volume products
claims.explanation: The one-page summary states U = 3 P_R V. This checks that algebraic identity without interpreting it as three independently stored energies.

claims.title: The supplied scalar response transforms to minus the length force
claims.explanation: Starting from the supplied coefficient of delta kappa in Eq. (9), the chain rule for kappa = c^2/L gives the coefficient -F_L of delta L. This checks the coordinate transformation, not the full action derivation.

consequences.title: One potential organizes the mechanical responses
consequences.text: Area change and acceleration-length change give the two coefficients of a single complete differential. Pressure is force per area, and the negative slope of surface stress. The checker can expose each dependence directly.

consequences.title: Radius work concerns the same Schwarzschild horizon
consequences.text: L = 2 R changes the work coefficient: radial pressure is twice length pressure. The equal-work identity describes a change in the same horizon’s areal radius and volume; it does not displace another surface at 2 R.

consequences.title: The action-response coefficient matches conditionally
consequences.text: Given the summary’s selected nonexpanding-null scalar response, the reciprocal-length substitution yields the same force coefficient as the potential derivative. Establishing the cited gravitational response itself remains outside these algebraic checks.

limitations: This is a prepared draft for author approval, based only on the one-page summary. It is not an author-approved submission or a verification of every statement in the manuscript.

The checker tests exact symbolic identities and mass–length–time dimensions under declared inputs. It does not provide a Lean proof, validate the physical inputs, establish novelty, or demonstrate agreement with experiment.

The boundary potential and selected gravitational response are physical inputs. Their canonical justification, admissible variations, and correspondence to the cited literature need expert review or a separate formal development.

The source uses positive surface gravity and positive acceleration length. Zero surface gravity, signed branches, unrestricted moving boundaries, rotation, and other sectors are not included in this package.

A and L are independent for partial derivatives. Schwarzschild A, L, and V co-vary only after substitution. The length pressure P_L is not generally the radial pressure P_R or a covariant bulk stress tensor; A L is not generally a volume.

The summary also discusses thermal translation and equilibrium FRW cosmology. Those claims are not tested by this initial package; no checked status here extends to their physical assumptions, Friedmann equations, or a complete moving-boundary theorem.
